## Reverse-engineering agent evaluation

[↑ Contents](#contents)

- [**Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14960) - Compares human and LLM-agent understanding and navigation on the same static reverse-engineering challenges, then studies how binary representations consume context windows. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Samuele Doria et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.14960) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-humans-machines-sre/)</sub>
- [**Training Language Model Agents to Find Vulnerabilities with CTF-Dojo**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/zhuo26c.html) - CTF-Dojo is an execution environment for training LLM agents on capture-the-flag tasks: 658 challenges from 50 competitions held between 2011 and 2025, taken from pwn.college's CTF Archive and containerized with Docker. <sub>ICML 2026 · Conference paper · Terry Yue Zhuo et al. · [PDF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v306/main/assets/zhuo26c/zhuo26c.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/amazon-science/CTF-Dojo) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-ctf-dojo/)</sub>
- [**The Next Challenge for Agentic Cybersecurity: A Realistic, Contamination-Free Reverse Engineering Benchmark**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11469) - Introduces SRE-Bench, with privately authored programs and protected binary variants, to study agent recovery of program semantics while reducing training-data contamination. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Jeremy Spence et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.11469) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-sre-bench/)</sub>
- [**Automatically Attacking Software Reverse Engineering AI Agents**](https://papers.academic-conferences.org/index.php/eccws/article/view/4597) - A proof of concept for indirect prompt injection against Cline/GhidraMCP binary-analysis agents. <sub>ECCWS 2026 · Conference paper · Brian Crawford et al. · [PDF](https://papers.academic-conferences.org/index.php/eccws/article/download/4597/4412/17540) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-attacking-re-ai-agents/)</sub>
- [**CrackMeBench: Binary Reverse Engineering for Agents**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10597) - Evaluates agents on executable-checked CrackMe tasks: infer validation logic from binaries and submit an accepted input or artifact, while recording tool use, time, and scoring attempts. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Isaac David et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.10597) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-crackmebench/)</sub>
- [**Towards LLM-Resistant Software Protection: Agent Failure Patterns in CTF Reverse Engineering**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/auto-draft-657/) - Runs Claude Code, Codex CLI and ChatGPT-5.2 Pro on 24 crackme-style challenges selected from 15 international CTF events held in 2025, and attributes their failures to stages of an Observe–Comprehend–Plan loop and to three protection effects: concealment, complication and misdirection. <sub>Workshop on Binary Analysis Research (BAR) 2026 · Conference paper · Ryutaro Nishizaka et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/bar2026-58.pdf) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-llm-resistant-protection/)</sub>
- [**ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs From Scratch?**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03546) - Evaluates black-box program reconstruction across 200 tasks: agents query an executable and read its documentation, then independently implement a codebase whose behavior is checked by generated tests. <sub>NeurIPS 2026 · Conference accepted · John Yang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.03546v1) · [Code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/ProgramBench) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-programbench/)</sub>
- [**Decompiling the Synergy: An Empirical Study of Human–LLM Teaming in Software Reverse Engineering**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/decompiling-the-synergy-an-empirical-study-of-human-llm-teaming-in-software-reverse-engineering/) - Studies how human analysts work with LLM assistance during static software reverse engineering. <sub>NDSS 2026 · Conference paper · Zion Leonahenahe Basque et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2026-f380-paper.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/mahaloz/dec-synergy-study) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-decompiling-synergy/)</sub>
- [**Cyber-Zero: Training Cybersecurity Agents without Runtime**](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/hash/f9f54762cbb4fe4dbffdd4f792c31221-Abstract-Conference.html) - Cyber-Zero synthesizes training trajectories for capture-the-flag (CTF) agents from public writeups instead of running the challenges. <sub>ICLR 2026 · Conference paper · Terry Yue Zhuo et al. · [PDF](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/file/f9f54762cbb4fe4dbffdd4f792c31221-Paper-Conference.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/amazon-science/Cyber-Zero) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-cyber-zero/)</sub>
- [**CREBench: Evaluating Large Language Models in Cryptographic Binary Reverse Engineering**](https://openreview.net/forum?id=tLYdf8hWJB) - Benchmarks cryptographic binary reverse engineering across algorithm recognition, key or IV extraction, wrapper reconstruction, and flag recovery using 432 controlled challenges. <sub>COLM 2026 · Conference paper · Baicheng Chen et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.03750v2) · [Code](https://github.com/wangyu-ovo/CREBench) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-crebench/)</sub>
- [**EnIGMA: Interactive Tools Substantially Assist LM Agents in Finding Security Vulnerabilities**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/abramovich25a.html) - EnIGMA extends SWE-agent for capture-the-flag challenges with interactive agent tools that keep a gdb debugging session or a pwntools server connection open across turns, alongside decompile and disassemble commands, an LM summarizer for long outputs, and category-specific demonstrations and guidelines. <sub>ICML 2025 · Conference paper · Talor Abramovich et al. · [PDF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v267/main/assets/abramovich25a/abramovich25a.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/tree/v0.7) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-enigma/)</sub>
- [**Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models**](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/3e9412a9c1d93810ef3ef7825115016b-Abstract-Conference.html) - Cybench turns 40 professional-level capture-the-flag tasks from four competitions (HackTheBox Cyber Apocalypse 2024, SekaiCTF 2022–23, GlacierCTF and HKCert) into runnable agent tasks. <sub>ICLR 2025 · Conference paper · Andy K. Zhang et al. · [PDF](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/3e9412a9c1d93810ef3ef7825115016b-Paper-Conference.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/andyzorigin/cybench) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-cybench/)</sub>
- [**NYU CTF Bench: A Scalable Open-Source Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating LLMs in Offensive Security**](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/69d97a6493fbf016fff0a751f253ad18-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.html) - NYU CTF Bench packages 200 manually validated challenges from CSAW CTF qualifying and final rounds held between 2017 and 2023, spanning cryptography, forensics, pwn, reverse engineering, web and miscellaneous tasks, with challenge.json metadata and Docker images for server-side challenges. <sub>NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks · Conference paper · Minghao Shao et al. · [PDF](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/69d97a6493fbf016fff0a751f253ad18-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/NYU-LLM-CTF/NYU_CTF_Bench) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-nyu-ctf-bench/)</sub>

## Decompilation and symbol recovery

[↑ Contents](#contents)

- [**Locate, Then Reason: End-to-End Patch Presence Testing in Stripped Binaries**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25071) - Locates patch-relevant code in stripped binaries using instruction-aligned retrieval and caller/callee context, then uses an LLM to screen candidate matches and compare patch-specific behavior with vulnerable and patched references. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Huaijin Wang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.25071v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-patchalign/)</sub>
- [**Recall-Oriented Precise Binary-to-Source Function Matching**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23546) - BScout matches decompiled functions to a source corpus using chunked embeddings and inlining-aware training. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Junlin Li et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.23546v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-bscout/)</sub>
- [**Decoding What iOS Location Services Send to Apple: An LLM Is an Unreliable Analyst but a Useful Toolmaker**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21597) - Compares direct LLM recovery of Apple PBCodable schemas with an AI-written Extractor checked against compiled synthetic fixtures, published descriptors and captured traffic. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Douglas Leith · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.21597v1) · [Code](https://github.com/doug-leith/ios-protobuf-decoding) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-ios-protobuf-extractor/)</sub>
- [**SoK: Are LLMs Reliable at Source Code Recovery? A Taxonomy and Empirical Evaluation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11556) - This SoK organizes LLM-assisted source-recovery designs and separates compilation, readability, structural and behavioral metrics. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Varun Kohli et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.11556v1) · [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/decompbench-65CB/) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-sok-source-recovery-reliability/)</sub>
- [**The CodeInverter Suite: Structure- and Data-Aware Binary Decompilation with Efficient LLMs**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3832783.3837554) - CodeInverter studies function-level LLM decompilation using control-flow graphs and memory-to-data mappings extracted with IDA/objdump. <sub>ASE 2026 · Conference paper · Peipei Liu et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.07215v3) · [Code](https://github.com/LiuPeiP-CS/CodeInverter) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-codeinverter-suite/)</sub>
- [**Beyond Text Matching: Towards Reference-Free Evaluation for Human-Oriented Binary Reverse Engineering**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3832783.3834339) - BinJudgeBench collects expert judgments for function naming, binary-code summaries and decompilation refinement. <sub>ASE 2026 · Conference paper · Xiuwei Shang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.07038v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-binjudge/)</sub>
- [**Decompiling Quantum Assembly into Structured Programs**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05012) - Quelle recovers library calls, loops, functions and symbolic parameters from compiled OpenQASM. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Pingchuan Ma et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.05012v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-quelle/)</sub>
- [**ASAP: Assembly-Source Aligned Pseudocode Refinement For Binary Decompilation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06900) - ASAP aligns assembly and source representations during training, compresses assembly features into tokens, and supplies them alongside decompiler pseudocode to an LLM refiner. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Yujian Zhuang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.06900v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-asap-decompilation/)</sub>
- [**Faultless: A Program Equivalence Technique for Validating and Evaluating Neural Decompilers**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34089) - Compares neural-decompiler C output with deterministic decompilation or reference functions using symbolic execution and a specialized memory model. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Luke Dramko et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.34089v1) · [Code](https://github.com/squaresLab/faultless) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-faultless/)</sub>
- [**Between the Commits: Process, Error, and Claim Reliability in a Wholly AI-Authored Codebase**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29744) - Studies development of the Extractor reverse-engineering tool through commits, available session logs and code-provenance tracing. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Douglas Leith · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29744v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-extractor-development-reliability/)</sub>
- [**Echo: Learning-based Matching Decompilation using Trusted Back Translation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18706) - Echo iteratively generates source and compiler configurations, recompiles candidates, and uses assembly differences to guide configuration search and code refinement. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Jun Bi et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.18706v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-echo-matching-decompilation/)</sub>
- [**A Memorization Floor for LLM Refinement of Decompiled Code**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17236) - Studies whether LLM refinement of decompiled C recovers identifiers from input evidence or prior knowledge. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Muhammad Asjad · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.17236v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-memorization-floor/)</sub>
- [**When LLM Decompilers Recompile More and Preserve Less**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05370) - Decompile-Diverge builds function-level behavioral comparisons from source-derived drivers and fuzzed reference inputs. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Chang Liu et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.05370v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-decompile-diverge/)</sub>
- [**Reveree: Diagnosing LLM Reverse-Engineering Agents**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01185) - Evaluates reverse-engineering agent traces through flag recovery, eight analysis milestones and action profiles. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Hadjer Benkraouda et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.01185v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-reveree/)</sub>
- [**Decoupling is a Necessity: Transformation-Agnostic Decompiled Code Recovery under Optimization and Obfuscation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27889) - ReSource refines decompiled functions affected by compiler optimization and obfuscation. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Zhiping Zhou et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.27889v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-resource/)</sub>
- [**STILL: Recovering Lowered STL Semantics for LLM-assisted C++ Decompilation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26408) - STILL predicts function-level STL container presence from stripped control-flow graphs and turns those predictions into compact hints for LLM refinement of Ghidra output. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Xiaohan Wang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.26408v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-still-stl/)</sub>
- [**The Evolution of Binary Decompilation in the Modern Era: A Taxonomy, Literature Review, and Future Perspectives**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24955) - This survey maps traditional, dynamic, matching and neural decompilation approaches, then organizes type recovery, control-flow restructuring, naming and refinement tasks alongside evaluation metrics and benchmark choices. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Omar Abusabha et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24955v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-evolution-binary-decompilation/)</sub>
- [**Lifting Optimized Binaries to Canonical Compiler IR via Structure-Aware Retrieval and Iterative Verification**](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.527/) - BRIDGE lifts stripped, optimized x86-64 and ARM64 functions, given as llvm-objdump disassembly, to LLVM IR. <sub>ACL 2026 · Conference paper · Xiaoao Zhu et al. · [PDF](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.527.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/Azhu-c/BRIDGE-rag) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-bridge-lifting/)</sub>

- [**MirrorCode: AI can rebuild entire programs from behavior alone**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30182) - Tests reimplementation of 25 command-line programs using execute-only reference access, documentation and visible examples. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Tom Adamczewski et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.30182v2) · [Code](https://github.com/epoch-research/MirrorCode) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-mirrorcode/)</sub>
- [**SoK: AI-Augmented Binary Reversing**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17398) - A systematization-of-knowledge survey of machine-learning, LLM and agentic approaches to binary reversing. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Yujeong Kwon et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.17398v2) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-sok-ai-binary-reversing/)</sub>
- [**Binary Decompilation LLM with Feedback-Driven Multi-Turn Refinement**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16162) - AutoDecompiler trains function-level decompilation models to revise assembly- or pseudocode-derived outputs using compilation, execution and I/O feedback. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Peipei Liu et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.16162v2) · [Code](https://zenodo.org/records/23120286) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-autodecompiler/)</sub>

Duck et al. · [PDF](https://comp.nus.edu.sg/~gregory/papers/e9patch.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/GJDuck/e9patch) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-e9patch/)</sub>
- [**RetroWrite: Statically Instrumenting COTS Binaries for Fuzzing and Sanitization**](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9152762) - RetroWrite statically rewrites 64-bit position-independent Linux binaries by generating reassembleable assembly, so instrumentation can be inserted as if at compile time. <sub>IEEE S&amp;P 2020 · Conference paper · Sushant Dinesh et al. · [PDF](https://hexhive.epfl.ch/publications/files/20Oakland.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/HexHive/retrowrite) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-retrowrite/)</sub>
- [**BinRec: Dynamic Binary Lifting and Recompilation**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3342195.3387550) - BinRec lifts an executable to LLVM IR from dynamic traces instead of static disassembly, then lowers the IR back to a recovered binary, so compiler passes can optimize, harden or otherwise transform it. <sub>EuroSys 2020 · Conference paper · Anil Altinay et al. · [PDF](https://download.vusec.net/papers/binrec_eurosys20.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/trailofbits/binrec-tob) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-binrec/)</sub>
- [**Egalito: Layout-Agnostic Binary Recompilation**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3373376.3378470) - Egalito statically recompiles stripped x86-64 and ARM64 binaries, using the metadata that position-independent executables and libraries carry to recover a complete disassembly in which every code and data cross-reference becomes an explicit link. <sub>ASPLOS 2020 · Conference paper · David Williams-King et al. · [PDF](https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~junfeng/papers/egalito-asplos20.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/columbia/egalito) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-egalito/)</sub>
- [**DIRE: A Neural Approach to Decompiled Identifier Naming**](https://doi.org/10.1109/ASE.2019.00064) - Combines lexical and structural information from decompiler output to predict meaningful variable names, with a training and evaluation corpus derived from compiled C projects. <sub>ASE 2019 · Conference paper · Jeremy Lacomis et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.09029) · [Code](https://github.com/pcyin/dire) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-dire/)</sub>
- [**Coda: An End-to-End Neural Program Decompiler**](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/hash/093b60fd0557804c8ba0cbf1453da22f-Abstract.html) - Coda decompiles the assembly of short functions into C in two phases. <sub>NeurIPS 2019 · Conference paper · Cheng Fu et al. · [PDF](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/file/093b60fd0557804c8ba0cbf1453da22f-Paper.pdf) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-coda/)</sub>
- [**Debin: Predicting Debug Information in Stripped Binaries**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3243734.3243866) - Debin predicts debug information for stripped ELF binaries on x86, x64 and ARM. <sub>ACM CCS 2018 · Conference paper · Jingxuan He et al. · [PDF](https://files.sri.inf.ethz.ch/website/papers/ccs18-debin.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/eth-sri/debin) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-debin/)</sub>
- [**rev.ng: A Unified Binary Analysis Framework to Recover CFGs and Function Boundaries**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3033019.3033028) - rev.ng lifts binaries to LLVM IR through QEMU's tiny code generator, so one front end covers every architecture QEMU supports and the output is compilable IR. <sub>CC 2017 · Conference paper · Alessandro Di Federico et al. · [PDF](https://nebelwelt.net/publications/files/17CC.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/revng/revng) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-revng/)</sub>
- [**Ramblr: Making Reassembly Great Again**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss2017/ndss-2017-programme/ramblr-making-reassembly-great-again/) - Ramblr produces reassembleable disassembly: assembly recovered from a stripped binary that can be edited and assembled again with an off-the-shelf assembler. <sub>NDSS 2017 · Conference paper · Ruoyu Wang et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/ndss2017_10-5_Wang_paper_0.pdf) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-ramblr/)</sub>
- [**No More Gotos: Decompilation Using Pattern-Independent Control-Flow Structuring and Semantics-Preserving Transformations**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss2015/ndss-2015-programme/no-more-gotos-decompilation-using-pattern-independent-control-flow-structuring-and-semantics/) - DREAM is a decompiler whose control-flow structuring recovers loops, conditionals and switch statements from a recovered control-flow graph without matching predefined region patterns. <sub>NDSS 2015 · Conference paper · Khaled Yakdan et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/11_4_2.pdf) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-dream/)</sub>

## Firmware analysis and rehosting

[↑ Contents](#contents)

- [**SoK: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Emulation-Based Dynamic Analysis Research for ARM Cortex-M Firmware (Extended Version)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38872) - Organizes 24 MCU analysis tools into configuration recovery, emulation, fuzzing and diagnosis stages, then evaluates the runnable, pipeline-compatible subset on 4,571 filtered Cortex-M firmware images. <sub>arXiv (extended version) 2026 · Preprint · Hongyuan Li et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.38872v1) · [Code](https://github.com/IoTS-P/LargeRehostingTesting) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-cortexm-emulation-sok/)</sub>
- [**POZZER: A Power Side Channel-guided Fuzzer for Black-Box Embedded Systems**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23583) - Builds a noise-tolerant pseudo execution-flow graph from one power trace per test input, using newly observed behavior as LibAFL feedback. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Pouya Narimani et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.23583v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-pozzer/)</sub>
- [**Reactive Peripheral Modeling for Faithful Firmware Rehosting**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29737) - Bluezz models peripherals as stateful event-condition-action systems, coordinating interrupts, MMIO and DMA rather than treating accesses independently. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Qinying Wang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.29737v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-bluezz-rpm/)</sub>
- [**Khost: KVM-based Near Native MCU Firmware Rehosting**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity26/presentation/wang-chunlin) - Extends KVM with MCU instruction handling, memory mapping and interrupt modeling to rehost firmware on ARMv8-A hosts. <sub>USENIX Security '26 2026 · Conference paper · Chunlin Wang et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity26-wang-chunlin.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/seclab-fudan/Khost) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-khost/)</sub>
- [**FirmPilot: Evidence-Guided Multi-Agent Environment Recovery for IoT Firmware Rehosting**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14903) - FirmPilot reconstructs QEMU execution environments through coordinated retrieval, planning, filesystem, persistent-state and network recovery. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Yanbing Shen et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.14903v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmpilot/)</sub>
- [**FirmCure:Towards Autonomous and Adaptive Rehosting of Linux-Based Firmware**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24549) - FirmCure combines static dependency analysis, iterative boot-configuration repair and runtime fault diagnosis to rehost Linux firmware in QEMU. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Chuan Hong et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.24549v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmcure/)</sub>
- [**SatBleed: Security of Commoditized Communication Modules in Satellites**](https://doi.org/10.1109/SP63933.2026.00213) - Studies satellite communication modules through hardware inspection, firmware reverse engineering, protocol analysis, partial rehosting and targeted testing. <sub>IEEE S&amp;P 2026 · Conference paper · Ulysse Planta et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.06258v1) · [Code](https://github.com/EmsecCispa/SatBleed) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-satbleed/)</sub>
- [**User-Space Dependency-Aware Rehosting for Linux-Based Firmware Binaries**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/user-space-dependency-aware-rehosting-for-linux-based-firmware-binaries/) - FIRMWELL reconstructs the execution environment of Linux firmware services by running their initialization processes, locating blocking dependencies and repairing missing system-level behavior. <sub>NDSS 2026 · Conference paper · Chuan Qin et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2026-s249-paper.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/qc9c/Firmwell) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmwell/)</sub>
- [**Target-Centric Firmware Rehosting with Penguin**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/auto-draft-634/) - Penguin rehosts embedded Linux firmware from an extracted filesystem by deriving an editable configuration of emulation transformations, such as file changes, pseudofiles, NVRAM values and network interfaces, from static analysis. <sub>Workshop on Binary Analysis Research (BAR) 2025 · Conference paper · Andrew Fasano et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/bar2025-final10.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/rehosting/penguin) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-penguin/)</sub>
- [**Fuzzware: Using Precise MMIO Modeling for Effective Firmware Fuzzing**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity22/presentation/scharnowski) - Rehosts monolithic ARM Cortex-M firmware for fuzzing, using locally scoped symbolic execution to model memory-mapped I/O accesses and focus input mutations on values relevant to firmware logic. <sub>USENIX Security 2022 · Conference paper · Tobias Scharnowski et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec22-scharnowski.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/fuzzware-fuzzer/fuzzware) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-fuzzware/)</sub>
- [**Jetset: Targeted Firmware Rehosting for Embedded Systems**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity21/presentation/johnson) - Jetset rehosts firmware only as far as an analyst-chosen goal address, such as the point where a fuzzer can inject input. <sub>USENIX Security 2021 · Conference paper · Evan Johnson et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec21-johnson.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/aerosec/jetset) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-jetset/)</sub>
- [**SoK: Enabling Security Analyses of Embedded Systems via Rehosting**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3433210.3453093) - Systematizes rehosting: moving embedded firmware from its physical hardware into a virtual environment that models enough hardware behavior for dynamic analysis such as fuzzing and symbolic execution. <sub>ACM ASIA CCS 2021 · Conference paper · Andrew Fasano et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3433210.3453093) · [Code](https://github.com/rehosting/rehosting_sok) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-rehosting-sok/)</sub>
- [**FirmAE: Towards Large-Scale Emulation of IoT Firmware for Dynamic Analysis**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3427228.3427294) - Extends Firmadyne with empirically derived interventions for boot, networking, NVRAM, kernel behavior, and other runtime failures, enabling Linux router and IP-camera firmware web services to run for dynamic analysis. <sub>ACSAC 2020 · Conference paper · Mingeun Kim et al. · [PDF](https://syssec.kaist.ac.kr/pub/2020/kim_acsac2020.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/pr0v3rbs/FirmAE) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmae/)</sub>
- [**HALucinator: Firmware Re-hosting Through Abstraction Layer Emulation**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity20/presentation/clements) - HALucinator rehosts monolithic ARM Cortex-M firmware by identifying hardware-abstraction-library functions and replacing them with authored Python handlers and peripheral models. <sub>USENIX Security 2020 · Conference paper · Abraham A Clements et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec20-clements.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/embedded-sec/halucinator) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-halucinator/)</sub>
- [**Towards Automated Dynamic Analysis for Linux-based Embedded Firmware**](https://doi.org/10.14722/ndss.2016.23415) - Firmadyne crawls, extracts and emulates Linux-based firmware for network-connected commercial devices such as routers and IP cameras. <sub>NDSS 2016 · Conference paper · Daming D. Chen et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/towards-automated-dynamic-analysis-linux-based-embedded-firmware.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/firmadyne/firmadyne) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmadyne/)</sub>
- [**Avatar: A Framework to Support Dynamic Security Analysis of Embedded Systems’ Firmwares**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss2014/ndss-2014-programme/avatar-framework-support-dynamic-security-analysis-embedded-systems-firmwares/) - Avatar runs embedded firmware in an instrumented emulator, S²E on QEMU, while forwarding memory-mapped I/O to the real device and injecting the device's interrupts back into the emulator, so firmware that depends on undocumented peripherals can still be analyzed dynamically. <sub>NDSS 2014 · Conference paper · Jonas Zaddach et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/02_3_1.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/avatarone/avatar-python) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-avatar/)</sub>

- [**BinaryInferno: A Semantic-Driven Approach to Field Inference for Binary Message Formats**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/binaryinferno-a-semantic-driven-approach-to-field-inference-for-binary-message-formats/) - Infers partial binary-message formats from static message samples without instrumenting an executable. <sub>NDSS 2023 · Conference paper · Jared Chandler et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/ndss2023_s131_paper.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/binaryinferno/binaryinferno) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-binaryinferno/)</sub>
